title: val and read-only collections
context: Does `val` make a collection immutable in Kotlin?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: No. `val` makes the reference unchangeable, not the object. `listOf` and `setOf` return read-only interfaces, so you can't call add on that type, but the object underneath may be mutable and may be changed through another reference. Use `listOf` for values you pass around, and copy into a new list before exposing internal state. If you need true immutability, use a copy, or a library with immutable collections.

points.title: Reference versus object
points.why: val stops reassignment of the variable, not changes to the object.

points.title: Read-only is not immutable
points.why: A read-only List type can still refer to a mutable list underneath.
